title: How To Be The Teacher Your Students Need
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin recounts observing a teacher whose classroom had descended into chaos despite having previously received step-by-step coaching on how to build a classroom management plan. He identifies the barrier not as lack of knowledge but as fear — specifically, fear that holding students accountable would cause them to rebel and turn the room into "sheer bedlam." His advice centers on fortitude: consciously shifting attention away from personal anxiety and toward how urgently students depend on their teacher to prepare them for a demanding world they don't yet understand. He argues that fear-driven inaction — looking the other way, bribing, giving up — sets students up for real failure and disappointment, while consistent accountability builds the trust, respect, and leverage that actually make teaching possible. The piece closes with a charge to teachers to see themselves as the "rescuer," "champion," and "leader" their students need, framed as a singular, non-repeatable opportunity to shape each student's future.
points: Knowing the strategies of good classroom management is not enough; fear of student rebellion often prevents teachers from applying them.
Consistent accountability, not avoidance, is what builds the trust, respect, and leverage that make effective teaching possible.
Shifting focus from personal anxiety to how urgently students depend on their teacher can dissolve paralyzing fear.
Fear-driven inaction — looking the other way, bribing, giving up — sets students up for real failure later in life.
Linsin frames teaching as a singular, non-repeatable opportunity to shape each student's future, urging teachers not to waste it.
quotes: Her classroom was chaotic. Her students played and goofed off. They yelled and roughhoused.
Because, you see, she was paralyzed by fear. She was afraid that if she held her students to a standard of behavior that was required for success in school, then they would rebel.
Consistent accountability is the foundation upon which trust, likability, and influence are built.

My advice to the teacher I observed that day is to take ‘you’ out of the equation. Turn down the volume on how you feel—your thoughts, worries, anxieties, and what ifs—and turn up the volume on how urgently your students need you.
So when you freeze up, when you look the other way, when you bribe and appease and give up and give in, you set them up for failure and crushing disappointment.
Your students need a rescuer, a defender, a role model, a lion, and a champion. They need a hero who will make a stand for them and their future.
This is your chosen career, after all, and you have but one chance to make an impact on each student that comes into your life. One opportunity. Don’t waste it.
